 Texas lawmaker wants to put security chips in Lone Star Cards to combat SNAP theft
 A new bill would require Texas to replace its outdated food assistance cards with more secure technology by 2029, following years of reports of stolen benefits
 Christian Hudspeth , Logistics Coordinator
 Published:  November 16, 2026 at 7:32 AM Tags:  Texas , SNAP , Lone Star Cards , Food Assistance , Skimming , Texas Legislature , Crime FILE - SNAP EBT information sign is displayed at a gas station in Riverwoods, Ill., Saturday, Nov. 1, 2025. (AP Photo/Nam Y. Huh, file) (Nam Y. Huh, Copyright 2025 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.) A Texas lawmaker wants to make it harder for criminals to steal food assistance benefits by requiring the state to equip Lone Star Cards with the same security technology commonly found in credit and debit cards.
 Sen. Judith Zaffirini, D-Laredo, filed Senate Bill 374 on Nov. 13. The legislation would require electronic benefit transfer (EBT) cards issued through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and the state’s cash assistance program to include security chips that allow users to insert or tap their cards instead of swiping them.

 The proposal comes after years of reports of criminals stealing SNAP benefits through a practice known as “skimming,” which involves capturing information from a card’s magnetic stripe and using it to make fraudulent purchases.
 Unlike most modern credit and debit cards, Texas Lone Star Cards still rely on magnetic stripes, leaving recipients vulnerable to this type of theft.
 KPRC 2 has extensively reported on the problem, including cases involving Houston-area families who discovered their food assistance benefits had been drained before they could purchase groceries.
 What would the bill change? 
 Under SB 374, the Texas Health and Human Services Commission would be required to transition Lone Star Cards to technology that offers greater protection against card skimming and cloning.
 The proposal establishes two deadlines:
 Sept. 1, 2028: Texas would begin issuing EBT cards equipped with security chips. 
 March 1, 2029: All EBT cards in use would be required to have the technology. 
 The chips would support both inserting a card into a payment terminal and contactless payments, commonly known as tap-to-pay.
 The legislation would also allow for a delay if federal approval or a waiver is necessary.
 The change would not increase or decrease the amount of SNAP benefits a household receives. Instead, it would change how recipients access and spend those benefits.
 Why is this necessary? 
 SNAP skimming has been a persistent problem in Texas, with criminals using devices attached to payment terminals to capture card information and personal identification numbers.
 The stolen information can then be used to create duplicate cards and drain recipients’ accounts, sometimes shortly after their monthly benefits are deposited.
 In April 2025, KPRC 2 reported on Claudette Merchant , a Houston mother of three whose SNAP benefits were stolen on the same day they were deposited onto her Lone Star Card.

 Merchant discovered the theft while attempting to buy groceries, leaving her with just a few dollars to feed her children.
 The problem has also drawn federal attention. In May 2025, KPRC 2 went inside a U.S. Secret Service investigation into SNAP skimming, where investigators demonstrated how criminals can capture card information and use it to commit fraud.
 Victims may not get their stolen benefits back 
 The proposed security upgrades are particularly significant because Texans whose SNAP benefits are stolen through skimming currently have no access to the previous federal replacement program.
 Congress temporarily authorized states to replace certain stolen SNAP benefits, but that authority expired in December 2024.
 According to Texas Health and Human Services, benefits stolen on or after Dec. 21, 2024, are not eligible for replacement under that program.
 That means families who lose their food assistance benefits to skimming may have to find other ways to purchase groceries until their next monthly payment arrives.
 The proposed legislation would focus on preventing theft rather than creating a new reimbursement program for victims.
 Federal government also considering security upgrades 
 Texas lawmakers are not alone in considering changes to EBT card security.
 In October, the U.S. Department of Agriculture published a proposed federal rule that would require states to transition SNAP cards to chip and contactless payment technology.
 Texas has new leaders. What’s next for TEFA, data centers and border security 
 The federal proposal would also establish additional security requirements for online transactions and give recipients more tools to monitor their accounts.
 The USDA said the changes are intended to reduce benefit theft caused by skimming and card cloning. The federal rule has not been finalized.
 What happens next? 
 SB 374 has been filed ahead of the Texas Legislature’s 2027 regular session, which begins Jan. 12.
 The proposal would need approval from both chambers of the Legislature and the governor’s signature before becoming law.
 If approved, the legislation would take effect Sept. 1, 2027, although the deadlines for issuing and replacing cards would come later.
 The cost of upgrading Texas’ EBT card system has not yet been established.
